sources.title: NGSS 5-PS2-1: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down
OpenStax University Physics Volume 1, 13.2 Gravitation Near Earth's Surface

note.text: Earth is a giant ball. Its gravity pulls on everything: you, a dropped ball, the ocean, even the air.

steps.title: Center
steps.instruction: Trace the dot at Earth's center.

note.text: A round planet pulls as if all its mass were at its center.

steps.title: Balls
steps.instruction: Trace the four balls dropped in different places.

note.text: Each ball is dropped by someone standing on a different part of Earth.

steps.title: Gravity's pull
steps.instruction: Draw the four arrows pointing toward Earth's center.

note.text: Every ball falls toward Earth's center. That direction is what we call down, wherever we stand.

steps.title: Label the model
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered part.

commonMistakes.North Pole: Gravity doesn't point toward the North Pole. It pulls toward Earth's center from everywhere.

steps.title: Argue
steps.question: A child on the other side of the world drops a ball. Which way does it fall?

options.text: Toward Earth's center, which is down for them
options.feedback: Yes. Gravity always pulls toward Earth's center, so down points at the center from every place on Earth.
Gravity pulls toward Earth's center from everywhere, so it falls down toward the ground.
Gravity pulls toward Earth's center, not toward any pole.
Look at the arrows: each points to the center. That's down for whoever drops the ball.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: Why don't people at the bottom of the globe fall off Earth?

options.text: Gravity pulls them toward Earth's center too
options.feedback: Right. There's no real bottom of Earth. Gravity pulls everyone toward the center, so their feet stay on the ground.
No holding needed: gravity pulls them toward Earth's center, just like us.

options.text: Gravity only works at the top
options.feedback: Gravity works all around Earth, always toward its center.
Shoes don't matter. Gravity pulls everyone toward Earth's center.
